### The King's All-Encompassing Reign
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/kings-all-encompassing-reign
Passage: Psalm 110:1-3
Points:
- Psalm 110 is the most frequently cited Old Testament passage in the entire New Testament.
- David calling his royal descendant "Lord" indicates the Messiah's deity and greatness over David himself.
- Making enemies a footstool depicts complete subjugation and uncontested royal dominion over all opposition.
- Christ's ascension marked the inauguration of the final defeat of every enemy opposing His kingdom.
- Because Christ cannot fail, believers united to Him by faith remain secure against every foe.

### Jesus According to the New Testament’s Most Quoted Psalm
Author: Justin Dillehay
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/psalm-110/
Passage: Psalm 110:1-4
Points:
- David overhears Yahweh speaking to David's Lord, foreshadowing the Messiah who is both David's descendant and God's Son.
- Christ's invitation to sit at the Father's right hand was fulfilled in His ascension to heavenly reign.
- Psalm 110 uniquely unites the offices of king and priest in a figure outside the Levitical line.
- Jesus was confirmed as high priest by a divine oath, making Him guarantor of a superior, unbreakable covenant.
- Unlike mortal earthly priests, Jesus exercises an eternal priesthood based on the power of an indestructible life.
